description: Every log line the services wrote (the gateway, the application and each extracted service), searchable by correlation ID. Provisioned from docker/grafana/dashboards/ecomdemo-logs.json - edits made in this UI are overwritten on reload.

list.description: Paste the X-Correlation-Id from a response header. Empty means no filter, so the panels below show everything.
list.label: Correlation ID
list.name: correlation_id

list.description: Which services' lines the panels below show. All by default, so a pasted correlation ID shows the whole request: the gateway's line, the application's and every service it reached (KI-070). Listed from the streams that carry a level label - only the JSON pipeline in docker/alloy/config.alloy sets one - so these are the services this repository builds, never PostgreSQL or Redis, and a new service appears here once it has logged.
list.label: Service
list.name: service

list.description: The log level, which Alloy promotes to a Loki label in docker/alloy/config.alloy.
list.label: Level
list.name: level

title: EcomDemo Logs

panels.title: Log lines per second, by level
panels.description: The shape of the log, not its content. Every selected service, stacked by level. A step change here is the fastest way to notice that something started going wrong, and an ERROR line appearing at all is worth a look - which is why `level` is a Loki LABEL and therefore cheap to group by.

panels.title: Errors in the selected window
panels.description: A count, not a rate: for errors the question is usually "were there any, and how many", and a rate of three errors an hour rounds to a flat line at zero.

panels.title: Lines for this correlation ID
panels.description: Zero with an ID pasted in means one of three things: the window does not contain the request, the ID was never issued, or Alloy is not shipping. The Alloy UI at http://localhost:12345 settles the third.

panels.title: Service log
panels.description: The lines themselves. With a correlation ID in the textbox at the top this is one request's whole story, in order, across every selected service (the gateway's request line first, then the application and each service it reached), including the lines Spring and Hibernate wrote during it - which is the thing that was impossible before this phase. The labels shown on each line say which service wrote it. The filter is `| correlation_id = "..."`, a STRUCTURED METADATA match rather than a label selector: see docker/alloy/config.alloy for why an ID must never become a label.

panels.title: Infrastructure log (the databases, Redis, Prometheus, Grafana: every stream without a level)
panels.description: The rest of the stack, shipped by the second pipeline in docker/alloy/config.alloy: every PostgreSQL (the monolith's and each extracted service's), Redis, Prometheus and Grafana. Selected as the streams WITHOUT a level label - only the JSON pipeline sets one - rather than by a list of names, so a container Alloy starts shipping appears here with no edit to this file (KI-071: the list here still named only db after the database split). Plain text, no parsing, no correlation - it is here because the explanation for an application error is sometimes a line PostgreSQL wrote a second earlier, and having to go and find it in `docker logs` is exactly the friction centralized logging removes.
